title: Arkadia Biotech - PII Flow, Prompt Ephemerality & Audit Walkthrough
summary: Arkadia wanted confirmation on prompt/content non-retention defaults, handling of PII/PHI, customer-managed KMS, RBAC/SSO mapping, and audit log details. Redwood team reviewed SOC 2/ISO posture, explained Private/VPC options, and committed to delivering SOC 2 report, KMS integration guidance, and an internal test plan for a short pilot. There was an ask for written 'no training' confirmation and a sample data deletion request flow.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-10-15 09:00 PT (16:00Z)
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Rachel Morgan (Redwood AE), Devon Li (Redwood SE), Priya Khandelwal (Redwood CSM); Dr. Elena Ruiz, Samir Patel, Maya Chen, Alex Torres (Arkadia)

[00:00:05] Rachel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Rachel, AE, we have Devon on the technical side and Priya for post-sales/compliance. how's everyone?
[00:00:15] Elena: Hi, thanks. we're looking to confirm a few things before we move to pilot around data handling, especially PII and PHI flows, and that prompts aren't used for re-training.
[00:00:25] Rachel: Totally, that's the agenda. Devon, do you want to take the tech bits?
[00:00:28] Devon: Sure. quick note, I'll try to stay high level and dig in where needed. Arkadia, maybe start with how you plan to send prompts and what class of data?
[00:00:40] Maya: Most will be clinical notes, some identifiers — so PHI in places. we need explicit controls. retention, encryption, and auditability are top of list.
[00:00:50] Samir: Also, single sign-on mapping and RBAC — we need role scoping so only certain users can call endpoints that return PHI.
[00:00:58] Devon: Understood. quick overview: Redwood's hosted API by default keeps minimal request records for observability for X hours, but we support configuration to reduce retention to ephemeral and we offer Dedicated and Private deployments where logs and data can be restricted further, including customer-managed K M S integration.
[00:01:16] Elena: When you say "minimal records" what's in the logs, like full prompt text or just metadata?
[00:01:22] Devon: Good question. default hosted observability includes request/response aggregates, token counts, and a short tracer id. by default we do not keep full prompt content beyond short-term buffers used for streaming. that said, in hosted mode we have options: you can opt out of content retention, enable prompt redaction in transit, or pick Dedicated/Private where you control retention policies.
[00:01:45] Maya: we need a written guarantee that customer prompts won't be used to train models. does Redwood have a policy?
[00:01:52] Rachel: Yes. our standard is that customer content is not used for training without explicit opt-in. i realize customers want something on letterhead. Priya will follow up with a formal statement.
[00:02:02] Priya: i'll draft a 'no-training' confirmation that references our data residency and retention defaults and point to the SOC 2 controls.
[00:02:08] Alex: is that on every tier, hosted included? some vendors say they're not training but then have clauses in t&c.
[00:02:15] Rachel: we can provide the exact clause. for hosted, the standard commercial terms include the no-training commitment; for enterprise Dedicated/Private we can make stronger contractual guarantees and include KMS BYOK and on-prem options.
[00:02:27] Samir: About KMS — we need customer-managed keys. can you do HSM-backed keys in our cloud?
[00:02:33] Devon: Yes. we support BYOK with major K M S providers — AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure KeyVault, and HSM workflows. you'll be able to bring keys and configure envelope encryption. integration details vary by deployment mode — in Private/VPC we can do direct KMS calls from your VPC. in Hosted we do a tokenized envelope approach.
[00:02:52] Elena: what's the default log retention window for request/response traces and audit logs?
[00:02:57] Devon: On hosted, audit trails retaining administrative actions are 90 days by default; request telemetry aggregates are 30 days. we can extend retention in Dedicated/Private; also we can provide a log export to your SIEM.
[00:03:10] Maya: 30 days for request content is too long if the content includes PHI unless we can redact. can the content be redacted at ingress?
[00:03:17] Devon: Yes, you can enable redaction at the SDK/proxy layer — we have pre-send hooks and regex-based scrubbers. also you can route through your own proxy in VPC or on-prem where you do the redaction yourself.
[00:03:29] Samir: And audit logs — do they contain the full prompt or just hashes?
[00:03:33] Devon: They contain metadata and optionally a hash of the payload; full content storage is opt-in. default hosted doesn't persist full content beyond streaming buffers. there are some legacy words in earlier docs that said otherwise, but that's been updated.
[00:03:48] Elena: SOC 2 and ISO — can you share the attestation and scope? we need control mapping for our auditors.
[00:03:55] Rachel: Absolutely. we'll send SOC 2 Type II report redacted and the ISO 27001 scope doc. i'll include a control mapping spreadsheet that maps your control IDs to Redwood controls.
[00:04:05] Alex: for SSO/SAML, do you support SCIM for provisioning and role push?
[00:04:09] Devon: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported. role mapping happens via claims — we map a SAML group to Redwood roles and you can customize via SCIM. small caveat: some older IdPs need a couple of extra claims, we'll share a sample mapping.
[00:04:22] Maya: how granular is RBAC? can we prevent devs from calling high-sensitivity models?
[00:04:28] Devon: You can assign model-level permissions and per-route policies. in Dedicated/Private you can also restrict endpoints by VPC IP ranges.
[00:04:36] Samir: If we go with Private deployment, do you still have any access to our logs?
[00:04:41] Rachel: On Private with customer-managed control plane, Redwood does not see your production logs by default. we can maintain an operational plane for updates but access is gated by customer approval and SSO.
[00:04:51] Elena: what's the deletion workflow? if we ask to purge old prompts, how quickly?
[00:04:56] Devon: We have a deletion API that will scrub stored prompts from the retention store; in hosted it's a 72-hour standard process once the deletion job is accepted — we have an escalation path for faster timelines for enterprise. in Private you control the storage so deletion is immediate per your process.
[00:05:10] Alex: will you show us an example call to the deletion API?
[00:05:13] Devon: yes, i'll include a snippet in the KMS/ops guide.
[00:05:16] Maya: for compliance we'll need proof the data wasn't used to train models historically. is there an audit trail for model training datasets?
[00:05:25] Priya: Good point. Redwood's training pipelines are segregated. customer data isn't in training datasets unless there's a bilateral agreement. we can provide attestations and the pipeline logs that show dataset sources for samples.
[00:05:36] Elena: i ask because some vendors have had accidental ingestion cases. we need to be able to demonstrate non-use.
[00:05:41] Rachel: understood. we'll include a statement and the relevant pipeline separation doc.
[00:05:45] Samir: Another question: data residency — we host in us-east for most of our app but clinical data needs to stay in eu-west. can you pin region?
[00:05:54] Devon: We support region pinning for Dedicated/Private. hosted model routing can also be restricted by region for certain accounts; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private in the target region.
[00:06:04] Elena: What about export controls — if some of our users are in Asia, do you limit cross-region replication?
[00:06:09] Devon: We can configure replication policies and cross-region backups can be disabled. again, Dedicated/Private gives full control.
[00:06:17] Maya: let's talk about PII detection. do you provide built-in PII detectors or should we do it before sending?
[00:06:22] Devon: We provide default PII detectors in SDKs — regex, ML-based detectors that can run client-side or server-side. for high-sensitivity PHI we recommend pre-send scrubbing in your sidecar.
[00:06:31] Alex: will detection logs themselves include fragments of PHI?
[00:06:34] Devon: Detection logs will include metadata and classification labels; fragments are not stored unless you enable that.
[00:06:40] Elena: For auditors, we'll need a walk-through of your audit log schema and retention options.
[00:06:46] Priya: we'll include a sample audit schema and a mapping to your auditors. plus an example export to Splunk/Datadog.
[00:06:53] Samir: Is there support for certificate pinning or mutual TLS for in-transit protection?
[00:06:58] Devon: Mutual TLS is supported for Private. Hosted supports TLS 1.3 with standard CA chains and we can do additional cert checks via our egress policies.
[00:07:08] Elena: Any known issues or gotchas we should be aware of for the pilot?
[00:07:12] Devon: Only that if you enable deep observability we might capture parts of text unless you enable redaction; so we'll default the pilot to scrubbed telemetry. also some older client libs need an update for SCIM group sync — we'll bring the patch.
[00:07:23] Rachel: Ok, let's recap next steps. we'll send SOC 2 and ISO docs, KMS guide, a written no-training confirmation, and sched a pilot kickoff.
[00:07:31] Elena: Thanks. one last thing — can you include a sample legal amendment for 'no training' so our legal team can review?
[00:07:37] Priya: yes, i'll include a suggested amendment and a redline-ready clause.
[00:07:42] Alex: Great. thanks everyone.
[00:07:45] Rachel: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links and the timeline.
[00:07:50] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription has some speaker bleed; technical terms like "KMS" were sometimes transcribed as "K M S" and "SAML" as "sam-el". There were a couple of truncated sentences when speakers crosstalked.
